reasoning: The proposal's exact research question -- whether standard post-hoc quantization alone (no fine-tuning, no adversarial prompting) revives knowledge removed by unlearning -- is the central, fully-established finding of "Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization" (arXiv:2410.16454, ICLR 2025). That paper shows unlearned models retain ~21% of forgotten knowledge in full precision but ~83% after 4-bit quantization, tested on WMDP with RMU-style methods and standard quantization tooling (GPTQ/AWQ, int8/int4), with a theoretical explanation that utility-preserving updates are too small to survive int4 discretization. The proposal's specific setup (RMU + WMDP forget set + off-the-shelf int8/int4) is essentially a smaller-scale replication, not a new contribution. Multiple 2026 follow-ups (e.g., arXiv:2602.13151 quantization-robust unlearning, arXiv:2605.15138, arXiv:2605.02196 DurableUn) further extend and confirm the effect.

evidence.title: Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization
evidence.summary: Directly answers the proposed question: applying standard post-hoc quantization to unlearned LLMs recovers forgotten knowledge. Reports forget retention rising from ~21% (full precision) to ~83% (4-bit), tested on WMDP with RMU-style methods and GPTQ/AWQ int4/int8, plus theory that utility-preserving updates are too small to survive int4 discretization. Published at ICLR 2025.

evidence.title: Quantization-Robust LLM Unlearning via Low-Rank Adaptation
evidence.summary: Follow-up work confirming int4 quantization systematically restores forgotten content even when models pass bf16 compliance audits, and proposing a mitigation. Demonstrates the problem is established and the field has moved to solutions.

evidence.title: DurableUn: Quantization-Induced Recovery Attacks in Machine Unlearning
evidence.summary: 2026 follow-up framing quantization-induced recovery as an attack vector against unlearning, further confirming the phenomenon the proposal sets out to test.

evidence.title: Forgetting That Sticks: Quantization-Permanent Unlearning via Circuit Attribution
evidence.summary: 2026 follow-up proposing quantization-permanent unlearning, treating quantization-induced knowledge recovery as a known established failure mode to defend against.
